- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.7) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 85), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at +3% above peak or use 3-period moving average for smoothing.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.3) and price is trending down, model often underestimates further decline; add 1–3% downward bias to forecast.
- Model frequently overreacts to sentiment shifts — if sentiment drops sharply, delay forecast adjustment until next 3-day window.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3-day average of forecast is > 82, reduce forecast by 1–2% per day until it aligns with 10-day moving average.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overestimate early in the period (first 5–7 days) — apply 1–2% downward correction to first 5 days of forecast.
- If sentiment is high but price is falling, model often ignores sentiment — adjust forecast downward by 1–3% for each day sentiment > 0.6 and price < 80.
